result: Chicken fibroblasts can proliferate stably in low-serum conditions, specifically in 1% chicken serum, with cell populations tripling in 3 days.
evaluation: Claims C14-C16 demonstrate that chicken fibroblasts maintain proliferation at reduced serum concentrations (6%, 3%, 1.5%) with decreasing rates, and specifically proliferate stably in 1% chicken serum with 3-fold expansion in 3 days. This is supported by EdU assay (Figure 1A-B) and CCK-8 assay (Figure 1C) data.

result: GelMA hydrogel scaffolds at different concentrations (3-9 wt%) exhibit varying porosity and structural properties, with 5% concentration identified as optimal for long-term chicken fibroblast culture.
evaluation: Claims C19-C24 provide comprehensive characterization of GelMA hydrogels showing inverse relationship between concentration and porosity (83.27% to 57.96%), pore sizes (3-100 μm²), and demonstrate that 3% hydrogel collapsed after 2 days while 5%, 7%, and 9% supported 9-day culture. The 5% concentration showed densest cellular structure. Data supported by SEM imaging (Figure 2A-B) and longitudinal observations.

result: Chicken fibroblasts in 3D culture multiply more than 15-fold by day 9 and show higher proliferation efficiency than 2D culture, indicating 3D provides a more favorable growth environment.
evaluation: Claims C25-C27 demonstrate superior cell proliferation in 3D versus 2D culture. PKH26 labeling (Figure 2C-D) quantified >15-fold expansion by day 9, and EdU assays (Figures 1B, 2E-F) showed gradually increasing proliferation rates in 3D that exceeded 2D levels. The conclusion that 3D is more favorable is directly supported by comparative data.

result: MyoD overexpression efficiently induces myogenic transdifferentiation of chicken fibroblasts in both 2D and 3D, with 3D culture achieving significantly higher fusion index (30.49%) and enhanced expression of myogenic markers compared to 2D.
evaluation: Claims C28-C34 establish that MyoD overexpression alone is sufficient for myogenic transdifferentiation, as serum deprivation caused cell death rather than improved differentiation (C29, Figure 3—supplement 2B). 3D culture produced abundant MHC+ multinucleated myotubes (C31, Figure 3B) with fusion index of 30.49% versus lower 2D levels (C32, Figure 3C). RT-qPCR data (Figure 3F) confirmed significant upregulation of MyoG, MYH6, MCK in both conditions, with MyoG and MCK significantly higher in 3D (C34).

result: MyoD-transdifferentiated cells express skeletal muscle markers (Desmin, Six1) and lose fibroblast markers (Vimentin, Thy-1) without expressing myofibroblast markers (α-SMA) or activating TGFβ signaling, confirming skeletal muscle lineage specification.
evaluation: Claims C35-C40 provide comprehensive lineage marker analysis demonstrating skeletal muscle identity. Immunofluorescence (Figure 4A-C) showed Desmin expression only in transdifferentiated cells (C35), α-SMA only in myofibroblasts (C36), and reduced Vimentin in transdifferentiated cells (C37). RT-qPCR (Figure 4D-F) confirmed elevated Desmin and Six1 (C38), reduced Thy-1 (C39), and unchanged TGFβ signaling components (C40), collectively ruling out myofibroblast differentiation.

result: Chicken fibroblasts undergo efficient lipogenesis in 3D culture when stimulated with fatty acids plus insulin or chicken serum, with 3D showing enhanced lipogenic gene expression compared to 2D.
evaluation: Claims C41-C48 demonstrate successful lipogenic induction. Optimization identified 8 μg/ml fatty acids + 60 μg/ml insulin as most efficient in 2D (C41, Figure 5—supplement 1). In 3D, extensive Oil Red O staining (C42, Figure 5B-C) and significantly elevated lipogenic genes (PPARγ, Gpd1, FABP4) were observed (C43-C44, Figure 5D). Znf423 increased only in 3D (C45), supporting enhanced 3D lipogenesis (C46). Both chicken serum (C47) and FI treatment (C48) significantly increased triglycerides (Figure 5E).

result: Sequential myogenic and lipogenic stimulation of the same cells produces myotubes with intramyocellular lipid deposition in both 2D and 3D, with both pathways activated independently without interference.
evaluation: Claims C49-C54 demonstrate successful dual differentiation. In 2D, MHC+ myotubes and Oil Red O+ lipids colocalized (C49), with lipids inside myotubes (C50, Figure 6—supplement 1C). Similar results in 3D (C51, Figure 6B-C). RT-qPCR showed significant upregulation of both myogenic and lipogenic genes (C52, Figure 6D), with comparable magnitude to single-pathway induction (C53), supporting the conclusion that pathways don't interfere (C54).

result: Lipogenic stimulation in 3D cultured meat achieves triglyceride levels comparable to or exceeding real chicken meat (1.5-7 mg/g range), with precise control through insulin and fatty acid concentrations.
evaluation: Claims C55-C57 demonstrate tunable fat content. Lipogenic induction increased triglycerides to levels matching/exceeding chicken breast and leg meat (C55, Figure 6E), while controls without lipogenic stimulation showed minimal triglycerides (C56). Dose-response experiments with varying insulin and fatty acid concentrations achieved precise triglyceride levels from 1.5-7 mg/g (C57, Figure 6E), overlapping and surpassing natural chicken meat ranges.

result: Collagen content in cultured meat gradually increases to 1.59 μg/mg, with dynamic changes in ECM gene expression (decreased COL1A1/COL1A2, increased fibronectin, stable elastin/laminin mRNA) and steady laminin protein accumulation.
evaluation: Claims C58-C62 characterize ECM dynamics. Total collagen reached plateau at 1.59 μg/mg (C58, Figure 7A). RT-qPCR showed decreased COL1A1/COL1A2 (C59), increased fibronectin (C60), and stable elastin/laminin gene expression (C61, Figure 7B). Despite stable laminin mRNA, protein accumulated steadily (C62, Figure 7C), indicating post-transcriptional regulation. Data are internally consistent and well-supported.

result: Transcriptome analysis reveals that myogenic/adipogenic transdifferentiation activates lineage-specific pathways (muscle organ development, PPAR signaling) and multifunctional pathways (JAK-STAT, NF-κB, MAPK), with 78% of DEGs in dual-stimulated cells overlapping with single-pathway stimulations.
evaluation: Claims C63-C69 present comprehensive transcriptome analysis. Hierarchical clustering (C63-C65, Figure 8B) showed 3D+FI distinct from others, 3D_MyoD and 3D_MyoD+FI similar, and 3D_fibroblasts separate. Venn diagram analysis confirmed 78% DEG overlap (C66, Figure 8D). GO analysis identified enriched myogenic (C67) and adipogenic (C68) pathways, plus multifunctional pathways (C69, Figure 8F) with literature support. RNA-seq data deposited (C106) enables verification.

result: 3D-cultured transdifferentiated myotubes are more organized and densely packed than 2D, resembling native myofiber distribution and producing meat-like appearance.
evaluation: Claims C103-C104 describe morphological improvements in 3D. Microscopy (Figure 3B) showed organized, densely packed myotubes resembling in vivo distribution (C103). Macroscopic comparison (Figure 3G) demonstrated meat-like appearance versus transparent empty scaffolds (C104). These qualitative assessments are supported by imaging data, though more quantitative metrics would strengthen the claims.

result: Control Tet-On-MyoD chicken fibroblasts without DOX treatment are indistinguishable from wild-type cells in morphology, proliferation, and gene expression.
evaluation: Claim C76 validates the inducible system. Figure 1—supplement 1A-C shows no differences between Tet-On-MyoD cells without DOX and wild-type cells in morphology, proliferation rate, and gene expression, confirming the system is tightly regulated and doesn't affect baseline cell properties.

result: Background claims establish that cultured meat offers environmental and ethical advantages over traditional farming, stem cells are difficult to scale, somatic cells can be converted to muscle, and fibroblasts are versatile cells suitable for cultured meat production with established protocols for myogenic and adipogenic conversion.
evaluation: Claims C1-C13 provide literature-supported background. Environmental benefits (C2-C4), stem cell limitations (C5-C6), somatic cell conversion potential (C7), fibroblast properties (C8-C9), and prior use in cultured meat (C10-C13) are all supported by appropriate citations. These establish rationale for the current study but are not novel findings.

result: GelMA hydrogel is established as a biocompatible, mechanically tunable scaffold commonly used in tissue engineering and cultured meat production.
evaluation: Claims C17-C18 and C83-C84 describe GelMA properties based on established literature (Pepelanova et al., 2018; Jeong et al., 2022; Zheng et al., 2021). These are background claims supporting material choice rather than novel findings.

result: Literature establishes that high intramuscular fat improves meat quality, co-culturing approaches can increase fat content, but adipocytes can impair myogenesis.
evaluation: Claims C71-C73 cite established literature on intramuscular fat effects (Gotoh et al., 2018; Motoyama et al., 2016), co-culture benefits (Lau et al., 1996; Pandurangan and Kim, 2015; Zagury et al., 2022), and adipocyte-myogenesis interference (Seo et al., 2019; Takegahara et al., 2014). These provide rationale for the sequential differentiation approach but are not novel findings.

result: Background claims establish MyoD as key myogenic factor, fibroblasts as common and versatile cells, their suitability for cultured meat (immortalization, low-serum adaptation), and FDA approval for commercial use.
evaluation: Claims C74-C75 and C77-C82 provide background on MyoD function (Ren et al., 2022; Weintraub et al., 1989), fibroblast properties, immortalization (Himly et al., 1998; Pasitka et al., 2023), serum adaptation (Genbacev et al., 2005; Lohr et al., 2009), and FDA approval (FDA, 2023). These establish context and feasibility but are not novel experimental findings.

result: The authors speculate that porous hydrogel structure may support multidirectional cell growth similar to in vivo myofiber formation.
evaluation: Claim C85 is explicitly stated as speculation without direct experimental validation. While the enhanced myogenesis in 3D is demonstrated (C32-C34), the specific mechanism involving porous structure enabling multidirectional growth remains hypothetical. Additional experiments (e.g., varying pore sizes, directional analysis) would be needed to test this hypothesis.

result: Background claims define molecular markers for myofibroblasts (MyoD, MHCs, α-SMA), skeletal muscle (Desmin, Six1), fibroblasts (Vimentin), and myogenic factors (MyoG, MYH6, MCK), plus TGFβ signaling in myofibroblast differentiation.
evaluation: Claims C86-C96 provide literature-supported definitions of cell lineage markers and signaling pathways (Hecker et al., 2011; Vaughan et al., 2000; Paulin and Li, 2004; Hinz et al., 2007; Tarbit et al., 2019; Relaix et al., 2013; Addison et al., 2014; Longo et al., 2018; Cao et al., 2006; van Rooij et al., 2009; Vincent et al., 1993). These are established knowledge used to interpret experimental results.

result: Literature establishes that JAK-STAT, NF-κB, and MAPK signaling pathways have profound effects on both myogenesis and adipogenesis.
evaluation: Claims C97-C102 cite established roles of multifunctional pathways in myogenesis (Bakkar and Guttridge, 2010; Jang and Baik, 2013; Keren et al., 2006) and adipogenesis (Batista et al., 2012; Bost et al., 2005; Richard and Stephens, 2011). These provide context for interpreting transcriptome results (C69) but are not novel findings.

result: The study received ethical approval and RNA-seq data are publicly deposited.
evaluation: Claims C105-C106 document ethical approval and data availability (PRJNA1102033). These are procedural statements that enhance reproducibility and transparency but are not scientific findings.
